title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 7: Lazarus analogy — no duty to raise all equally
pass_a_gloss: Just as therefore this argumentation would be inept: If Christ acting on earth raised dead Lazarus to life from the mere good pleasure of his will, and not from foresight of any cooperation on Lazarus's part, then he would have raised all the dead equally, because all had been equally disposed to receive this gift of resuscitation; so also that prior [argument] of Gregory is invalid and inept; because it assumes an obligation in God, that as often as he acts from good pleasure, he act alike with equals; and because it posits a common disposition in human beings to receive the gift of election, who are commonly disposed to receive the punishment of damnation.
pass_b_english: Just as it would be inept to argue: if Christ on earth raised dead Lazarus from mere good pleasure of his will, not from foresight of any cooperation on Lazarus's part, then he would have raised all the dead alike, because all were equally disposed to receive that gift of raising — so Gregory's prior argument is invalid and inept. It assumes God is bound, whenever he acts from good pleasure, to deal alike with equals; and it posits a common disposition to receive election in people who are commonly disposed to receive damnation's punishment.
source_text: Sicuti ergo inepta esset haec argumentatio, Si Christus in terris agens mortuum Lazarum resuscitavit ad vitam ex mero beneplacito voluntatis suae, et non ex praevisione alicujus cooperationis ex parte Lazari, tum omnes mortuos ex aequo resuscitasset, quia omnes aeque dispositi fuerant ad hoc donum resuscitationis recipiendum; sic etiam et prior illa Gregorii invalida et inepta est; quia supponit obligationem in Deo, ut quoties agit ex beneplacito, agat pariter cum paribus; et quia ponit communem dispositionem in hominibus ad recipiendum donum electionis, qui sunt communiter dispositi ad recipiendam poenam damnationis.
